from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        config.no_latex_cleanup = True
        lecture_lines = [
            "Complex numbers are points in the plane.",
            "Holomorphic functions define geometric mappings.",
            "Consider the simple map f(z) equals z squared."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisites & The Complex Plane", lecture_lines)
        
        # Complex plane objects
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        axes.get_x_axis().set_color("#00CED1")
        axes.get_y_axis().set_color("#FF4500")
        grid = NumberPlane(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3], background_line_style={"stroke_color": "#D3D3D3", "stroke_width": 1})
        
        # Define complex number z
        z = complex(1.5, 1.0)
        z_point = Dot(axes.c2p(z.real, z.imag), color=WHITE)
        z_label = MathTex("z", color=WHITE).next_to(z_point, UR, buff=0.1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(grid), Create(axes))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(z_point), Write(z_label))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Concept of Iteration", [
            "Iteration means repeatedly applying the same function.",
            "Orbits trace the path of a starting point.",
            "Simple rules create complex, dynamic sequences."
        ])
        
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-2, 2, 1], y_range=[-2, 2, 1], x_length=5, y_length=5)
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.add(axes)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        z0_dot = Dot(color="#FFFFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(z0_dot, 'C3')
        z0_label = MathTex("z_0 = 0").next_to(z0_dot, UP)
        self.play(Create(z0_dot), Write(z0_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFA500"))
        
        # Iteration path
        c = complex(-0.5, 0.5)
        z = 0
        points = [z]
        for _ in range(5):
            z = z**2 + c
            points.append(z)
            
        dots = VGroup()
        for p in points:
            dot = Dot(axes.c2p(p.real, p.imag), color="#FFA500", radius=0.06)
            dots.add(dot)
            
        self.play(FadeIn(dots))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        
        path = VMobject(color="#00FF00", stroke_width=2)
        path.set_points_smoothly([axes.c2p(p.real, p.imag) for p in points])
        self.play(Create(path))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Fixed points satisfy the equation f(z) equals z.",
            "Derivatives determine the stability of these points.",
            "Attractors pull nearby points into their orbit."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Fixed Points and Stability", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Fixed points satisfy the equation f(z) = z.
        # Highlight: Fixed point circle (blue)
        fixed_pt = Circle(radius=0.2, color="#1E90FF", fill_opacity=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(fixed_pt, 'B3')
        label_f = MathTex("f(z)=z").next_to(fixed_pt, UP, buff=0.1)
        self.play(FadeIn(fixed_pt), Write(label_f))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#1E90FF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Derivatives determine the stability of these points.
        # Highlight: Unstable fixed point X (red)
        unstable_pt = Cross(color="#FF0000", scale_factor=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(unstable_pt, 'E3')
        label_u = Text("Unstable", font_size=18, color="#FF0000").next_to(unstable_pt, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        self.play(FadeIn(unstable_pt), Write(label_u))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF0000")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Attractors pull nearby points into their orbit.
        # Highlight: Orbit converging (green)
        orbit_dot = Dot(color="#00FF00")
        start_pos = self.grid['B5']
        orbit_dot.move_to(start_pos)
        
        self.add(orbit_dot)
        self.play(
            orbit_dot.animate.move_to(fixed_pt.get_center()),
            run_time=2,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Julia Set: The Boundary of Chaos", [
            "The Julia set is a chaotic boundary.",
            "Iterates of points diverge at this edge.",
            "Stability defines the surrounding Fatou set."
        ])
        
        # Create visual elements
        # Using simple geometric representation for the Julia set concept
        points = VGroup(*[Dot(radius=0.04) for _ in range(100)])
        self.place_in_area(points, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        boundary = VMobject()
        boundary.set_points_smoothly([self.grid["B3"], self.grid["B4"], self.grid["C5"], self.grid["D5"], self.grid["E4"], self.grid["E3"], self.grid["D2"], self.grid["C2"]])
        boundary.set_stroke(color=YELLOW, width=4)
        self.add(boundary)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(points), FadeIn(boundary))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Points escape to infinity (visualize as fading to dark blue)
        escaping = VGroup(*[points[i] for i in range(len(points)) if i % 3 != 0])
        self.play(escaping.animate.set_color("#00008B"))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(BLUE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Remaining points define the Fatou set (stability)
        stable = VGroup(*[points[i] for i in range(len(points)) if i % 3 == 0])
        self.play(stable.animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(1)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["The Mandelbrot set maps all possible Julia sets.", 
                         "The parameter c controls the dynamical system.", 
                         "Small changes in c drastically alter behavior."]
        self.setup_layout("Application: The Mandelbrot Set", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Representing C-space
        plane = ComplexPlane(x_range=[-2.2, 1, 1], y_range=[-1.5, 1.5, 1]).scale(0.5)
        self.place_in_area(plane, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(plane), self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Representing "c"
        dot = Dot(color=ORANGE)
        label = MathTex("c", color=ORANGE)
        self.place_at_grid(dot, 'C3')
        self.place_at_grid(label, 'C4')
        self.play(FadeIn(dot), Write(label), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(ORANGE))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Final shape (Mandelbrot set sketch)
        mandelbrot = Mobject() # Placeholder for visual representation
        # Actually drawing a Mandelbrot-like shape
        m_shape = VMobject(color=WHITE)
        m_shape.set_points_smoothly([self.grid['B3'], self.grid['B4'], self.grid['D5'], self.grid['E3'], self.grid['D2'], self.grid['B3']])
        m_shape.set_fill(WHITE, opacity=0.5)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(m_shape), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Introduction to Holomorphic Dynamics: Iterating Complex Functions

sections.title: Prerequisites & The Complex Plane
sections.content: Briefly define the complex plane (z = x + iy) and the concept of a holomorphic function (differentiable in the complex sense). Visualize the domain as a mapping space.
sections.example: Visualizing f(z) = z^2 as a geometric transformation that squares the modulus and doubles the argument.

sections.title: The Concept of Iteration
sections.content: Introduce function iteration: f^n(z) = f(f(...f(z)...)). Explain the behavior of orbits—the sequence of points generated by repeatedly applying the function to an initial seed.
sections.example: A 'Digital Frog' jumping on the complex plane; where it lands after 1, 2, or 10 jumps based on the rule f(z) = z^2 + c.

sections.title: Fixed Points and Stability
sections.content: Define attracting, repelling, and neutral fixed points. Use the derivative |f'(z)| to determine if a point 'sucks in' or 'pushes away' nearby orbits.
sections.example: A whirlpool (attractor) vs. a mountain peak (repeller) in a complex landscape graphic.

sections.title: The Julia Set: The Boundary of Chaos
sections.content: Introduce the Julia Set as the set of points where the behavior of iteration is sensitive to initial conditions. Contrast this with the Fatou Set (stable regions).
sections.example: A 'Complex Maze' boundary: points inside are safe, points outside escape to infinity, and the boundary itself forms a complex fractal.

sections.title: Application: The Mandelbrot Set
sections.content: Summarize how the Mandelbrot set acts as a 'dictionary' of all possible Julia sets, showing how changing a parameter 'c' shifts the dynamics entirely.
sections.example: A 'Universal Controller' dial: Turning the knob 'c' morphs the shape of the Julia set dynamically, illustrating the connectivity of holomorphic dynamical systems.
